name: Coral bleaching
summary: No new global bleaching event declared as of 12 Nov; El Niño heat stress threatens Caribbean reefs
state: NOAA said in June that the fourth global bleaching event had likely ended in late 2025, and no fifth event had been declared as of 12 Nov (Sierra Club, 23 Sep). NOAA's August outlook gave a greater than 70% chance of Alert Level 1 heat stress across most of the Caribbean by early November (GCRMN, 14 Aug), and scientists warned the strong El Niño could bring another global event. No confirmed regional mass-bleaching report was found as of 12 Nov, so the level stays Normal with an upward trend.
for_you: Reef-dependent fisheries and tourism in the Caribbean and Pacific are most exposed if bleaching develops. Effects on reefs usually show up weeks after heat stress peaks.
rubric_hit: Normal: no global bleaching event in progress as of 12 Nov

sources.title: Sierra — Corals face an existential threat as the super El Niño heats up
CORDAP — Will the El Niño bring a fifth global coral bleaching event?

why: Reefs support a quarter of marine species and coastal economies; mass bleaching is a direct sign of ocean heat stress.
drivers: Marine heatwaves, El Niño, warming trend.
